title: Shopify channel mapping: what it covers, and when product data should live in a PIM
summary: Shopify channel mapping sends different product data to each sales channel. See what you can and can't map, and when your master record belongs in a PIM.
body_markdown:
On October 28, 2026, Shopify[added channel mapping to the admin](https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/map-product-data-by-sales-channel) . It is a single channel mapping page. You choose each sales channel on that page, including Shopify Catalog, and preview the data that channel receives. The release also added per-product overrides, bulk editing of channel values, and a coverage score for every channel field.


This guide covers what Shopify channel mapping can and can't map, and which AI channels it reaches through Shopify Catalog. It then explains when Shopify can hold the master record on its own, when the master record belongs in a PIM, and how the two fit together.


## What Shopify channel mapping is


Channel mapping is a set of rules that decides which field in your store supplies each field a sales channel receives. One product record can carry a short, brand-led title on the storefront and a longer title with color, material and size for a shopping feed or an AI channel.


As[Shopify's channel mapping help page](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-sales-channels/channel-mapping) explains, a field mapping applies to every product you publish to that channel. Product details on your online store stay the same.


## What you can map with Shopify channel mapping


Channel mapping works with sales channels that use contextual product data, and Shopify names Google & YouTube and Facebook & Instagram as examples. Most sales channels are eligible. The same mapping page also covers Shopify Catalog. Shop and Shopify Collective are not eligible.


- **Sources:** A channel field can draw from a product field, a variant field or a metafield. Only sources whose data type the field accepts are offered.
- **Empty-field fallback:** If the source field a channel points to is empty for a product, that product uses the channel's default source instead. The same rule applies to Shopify Catalog.
- **Combined values:** Single-line and multi-line text fields can join sources with typed text. Adding the brand name to the product title is a typical use.
- **Liquid:** You can write a channel field's value as Liquid code instead of using the visual editor, with up to 10 sources per value. Liquid tags such as` if` ,` for` and` assign` are not supported.
- **Per-product overrides:** You can enter a different value for one product or variant on one channel through the bulk editor. Shopify's channel mapping help page lists which field types can take an override.
- **Field coverage:** Each channel field shows the percentage of products that have a value, so gaps are visible before the feed goes out.


## What you can't map with Shopify channel mapping


- **Prices:** Money fields, including price, can't be used as a mapping source. Different prices per region are set in Shopify Markets, which supports[percentage price adjustments and prices set by country or region](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/pricing) .
- **Mappings by product category:** A channel's mapping covers the whole channel. You can't give one product category its own mapping.
- **Combined media and unstructured metafields:** Only text fields can combine values. Media fields can't, and unstructured metafields can't be part of a combined value.
- **Every channel:** Shop and Shopify Collective are not eligible for channel mapping.


## Channel mapping for Shopify Catalog and AI channels


### Which AI channels Shopify Catalog supplies


AI channels are a separate list from the sales channels you map.[Shopify's agentic storefronts page](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-sales-channels/agentic-storefronts) lists ChatGPT, Google AI Mode and Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, and Meta as AI channels. Every one of them requires your products to be eligible for Shopify Catalog, and each sets its own further requirements, such as the countries you sell to.


Shopify names ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot as AI channels that find products through Shopify Catalog. For Google AI Mode, Gemini and Meta, Shopify points to its own sales channels. According to[Shopify's guide to Catalog and product discovery](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-sales-channels/agentic-storefronts/products) , products reach Google AI Mode and Gemini through the Google & YouTube sales channel, and Meta surfaces through the Facebook & Instagram by Meta sales channel.


So the Shopify Catalog mapping sets the product data that ChatGPT and Copilot draw on. For Google AI Mode, Gemini and Meta, the mappings for the Google & YouTube and Facebook & Instagram channels matter too. Google Merchant Center is another route for Google.


### Options only Shopify Catalog has


When you select Shopify Catalog on the mapping page,[Catalog mapping](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-catalog/mapping) adds two options that ordinary sales channels don't have.


- **Custom variant grouping:** Combines separate products into one listing, keyed on a title delimiter, a product metafield or a tag prefix.
- **List price:** Sends either the current price or the compare-at price. Compare-at is used only when it is higher than the current price.


### Grouping limits and preview


Most grouping methods allow up to 10,000 products in a group. A product reference list metafield allows 1,024 per group and up to 100,000 products across all the groups it creates. Shopify notes that its preview does not show exactly how AI channels will display your data.


### How agents use Catalog data


Agents also search this Catalog through[Shopify Shop MCP](https://www.hypotenuse.ai/blog/shopify-shop-mcp) . The titles, descriptions and variant groupings you set for Catalog are the data those agents match against.


## When Shopify works as the master catalog


Channel mapping lets one Shopify product record feed every eligible sales channel, and Shopify Catalog for AI channels, with each channel reading the fields it needs. Because Shopify can syndicate one record this way, it can serve as the master record. That holds only when every value each channel needs already exists in Shopify and is created and approved there.


Shopify works as the master record when these conditions apply:


- **One store:** A single Shopify store carries the full assortment, so there is one record per product.
- **Data created in Shopify:** Your team writes and edits product data directly in the Shopify admin, rather than receiving it from suppliers.
- **Channel needs covered by existing fields:** Each channel's requirements can be met by product fields, variant fields, metafields and combined values already in the store.
- **Review inside Shopify:** Shopify roles and staff permissions are enough to control who edits and publishes product data.


In this setup, metafields hold the channel-specific attributes and channel mapping decides which ones each channel reads.


## When the master record belongs in a PIM


Channel mapping only distributes values that already exist in Shopify. It does not create those values, collect them from suppliers, route them for approval, or send them to systems outside Shopify. When your product data needs that work before it reaches Shopify, Shopify can't be the master record. A PIM for Shopify holds it instead and passes finished values to Shopify.


A PIM fits when one or more of these apply:


- **Several stores or platforms:** Mapping rules live inside each store's admin, so they can't keep several Shopify stores, marketplaces and B2B portals consistent. A master record outside any single store can.
- **Supplier data:** Spreadsheets, PDFs and portal exports need mapping to your attribute model and normalizing. Channel mapping works only with data already in Shopify fields.
- **Approvals:** Sign-off from merchandising, compliance or brand teams needs a review workflow and an audit trail on each value. Channel mapping has no approval step, and its staff permissions only control who can view or edit mappings.
- **Several markets and languages:** Localized attributes and copy per region are easier to manage from one record with market-specific versions.
- **Requirements beyond Shopify:** Marketplaces each set their own required fields, as our breakdown of[product attributes by channel](https://www.hypotenuse.ai/blog/product-attributes-by-channel) shows. A PIM holds the full set, and Shopify receives the part it needs.


## How a PIM and channel mapping work together


The PIM owns the master record and the approval process. Its job on the Shopify side is to write approved values into Shopify product fields, variant fields and metafields. Channel mapping then decides which of those fields each channel reads.


Here is a worked example. The storefront title stays in the product title field. The PIM writes an approved, attribute-rich feed title to a product metafield, and the Google & YouTube and Shopify Catalog title fields are mapped to that metafield. When a title is changed and approved in the PIM, the sync updates the metafield and Shopify refreshes each channel's feed.

## FAQ


### Can you set different prices per sales channel with Shopify channel mapping?


No. Money fields, including price, can't be used as a mapping source. For Shopify Catalog, you can choose whether the current price or the compare-at price is sent as the list price. Price differences by region are handled in Shopify Markets.


### Does channel mapping change product pages on the online store?


No. Channel mapping changes only what each sales channel receives. Titles, descriptions and other details on your online store stay as they are in the product record.


### Which sales channels support channel mapping?


Sales channels that use contextual product data support channel mapping, and Shopify names Google & YouTube and Facebook & Instagram as examples. Most sales channels are eligible, but Shop and Shopify Collective are not. Shopify Catalog is mapped from the same page and has extra options. Catalog in turn supplies AI channels such as ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot.


### Is Shopify channel mapping available on every plan?


Shopify's channel mapping help page does not list a plan restriction, and Shopify states that all stores can customize their data for Shopify Catalog. Getting products into Catalog is separate, and Catalog has its own store and product eligibility rules.
